name: two-hour-throttle-intermediate-reversion
rationale: Combines the two parameter changes that each independently improved both diagnostic capitals: two-hour block + two-hour spacing (7200/7200; 2026-09-25: 500,000 JPY Sharpe -16.69 -> +3.00) and the intermediate reversion horizons rsi 60 / bollinger 90 (2026-09-28: 500,000 JPY Sharpe -17.36 -> -7.46 with a monotone dose-response across 42/60 -> 60/90 -> 90/120). Literature (arXiv:2608.21888) finds short-horizon crypto reversion is real but its gross edge (~1.3bp) is far below round-trip cost (~5bp), which argues for keeping the reversion-dominated signal while trading it much less often and on a slightly slower horizon -- exactly this combination. Never tested jointly; the risk is that the two throttles compound into too few trades at 50,000 JPY, which must be reported rather than read as evidence against the signal.

paper_reference.title: Short-horizon mean reversion in cryptocurrency markets: a matched cross-market measurement
paper_reference.authors: Nadav A. Kitron, Jonathan M. Wengrowicz
paper_reference.key_claim: At a 15-minute horizon, 90% of 183 Binance pairs show significant directional reversal (vs 2.7% of US stocks), concentrated after taker-driven moves, but the gross edge (~1.3bp per trade) is too small to clear ~5bp round-trip spot costs.
paper_reference.pros: Independently corroborates shirube's own finding that the mean-reversion family is the only sub-signal family with any value at 1-minute resolution, and its cost conclusion matches shirube's measured fee/slippage domination (fee_drag_pct exceeding total_return_pct at every capital that trades).
paper_reference.cons: Binance pairs, not bitFlyer BTC/JPY; contrarian bet on the prior candle rather than an RSI/Bollinger composite; no lot-size minimum; descriptive measurement, not an allocation rule. Used only to motivate throttling action while keeping the reversion signal, not to pick parameter values.
